title: The Cauchy Problem in General Relativity
version: EMS Press / ESI Lectures in Mathematics and Physics, 2009, DOI 10.4171/053, ISBN 978-3-03719-053-1
locators: Chapter 13 The constraint equations (13.3 scalar-field case), Chapter 14 Local existence (14.2 Initial data p. 154; 14.3 Existence of a globally hyperbolic development = Theorem 14.2, p. 156; 14.4 Two developments are extensions of a common development = Theorem 14.3, p. 158), Chapter 16 (Theorem 16.6, p. 177, erroneous proof, see errata). Interior proof pages 152-163 and 176-183 NOT accessed; statements verified via the author's correction note verbatim restatements (scalar-ext-ringstrom-mghd-note), the free Introduction chapter (ems.press/content/book-chapter-files/19851: 'we shall restrict our attention to the non-linear scalar field case'), and the detailed contents file (ems.press/content/book-chapter-files/19850).
relevance: Published source for the coupled field-preserving local existence (Theorem 14.2) and common-GHD-extension (Theorem 14.3) theorems for the Einstein-nonlinear scalar field system; V=0 is exactly the task's massless system after the linear rescaling phi_R = sqrt(2) phi_T.
assumptions: Initial data per its Definition (restated as correction-note Definition 2.1): smooth data on an n-dimensional manifold Sigma, no compactness/completeness/asymptotic condition; scalar constraints; time-oriented GH developments.
conclusion: Existence of a GHD of given smooth data (Thm 14.2); any two developments of the same data admit a common GHD with time-orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms onto their images pulling back both the metric and the scalar field (Thm 14.3).
proof_status: Statement verified verbatim via author restatement; interior proofs not independently audited (access gate recorded in RESULT.md section 6).
open_questions: Whether the book's Ch.14 function-space machinery restricts Sigma (contents suggest no restriction in the statement)
limits: Book interior not read (no lawful access). Reliance on author-verbatim restatement chain is explicit. No errata item touches pp. 147-163.

title: Existence of a Maximal Globally Hyperbolic Development
version: Author web document, undated, linked from the book errata page (accessed 2026-10-29); no arXiv or journal version found
locators: Sec. 2: equations (2)-(3) [Ric - dphi x dphi - (2/(n-1))V(phi) g = 0; wave_g phi - V0(phi) = 0], Definition 2.1 (initial data, general smooth manifold), Remark 2.2 + Theorem 2.3 (= book Thm 14.2), Theorem 2.4 (= book Thm 14.3, field-preserving common development: psi_j^* g_j = g and psi_j^* phi_j = phi), Definition 2.5, Definition 2.7 (field-preserving isometric embedding), Lemma 2.8; Sec. 6: Definition 6.1 (class C(M,Mhat)), Remark 6.2, Lemma 6.4 (unique maximal element; pinpoints the book error at [8, p.178, l. -14/-13]), Definition 6.7 (common extension with metric gtilde and function phitilde), Lemma 6.10 (Hausdorff common extension is a GHD into which both developments embed), Sec. 9-10: Corollary 9.3, Lemma 9.4, Lemma 10.1 (common extension is Hausdorff), Corollary 10.2 (MGHD existence). References: [3] CBG 1969, [7] O'Neill (Lemma 40 p. 423; Lemma 21 p. 412; Proposition 62 p. 91 as cited by the note), [8] the 2009 book.
relevance: The corrected, coupled proof of record. Theorem 2.4 supplies Theorem A(a); Def 6.1 + Lemma 6.4 + Def 6.7 + Lemma 6.10 + Lemma 10.1 supply Theorem A(b), the coupled analogue of Sbierski's vacuum Theorem 2.7, with field preservation throughout (psi^* phi = phihat at every step).
assumptions: Smooth Einstein-nonlinear scalar field system, smooth initial data on a general manifold; developments time-oriented; local existence/uniqueness as in the book's Chapter 14.
conclusion: Two coupled GHDs of the same data admit a common GHD containing both, with field-preserving isometric embeddings; hence an MGHD exists (Cor 10.2) and is unique up to field-preserving isometry (Lemma 2.8).
proof_status: Statements extracted verbatim; proof of Lemma 10.1 read in its opening only, not re-derived; Sections 7-8 read at statement level. Uses the axiom of choice (Theorem 3.4/Zorn) openly.
open_questions: Dezornified (choice-free) coupled common-extension proof would remove Zorn; vacuum-only dezornification (Sbierski) does not cover the field
limits: Unrefereed author web document, undated; version pinning is by URL and content hashes of quotes. Uses Zorn's lemma for the maximal common piece.

title: On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification
version: arXiv:1309.7591, ar5iv rendering cross-checked against the v3 quotes in screening-repair-review/REVIEW_COMMON_EXTENSION.md (v3 dated 2 July 2015); published DOI 10.1007/s00023-015-0401-5 (pagination not consulted)
locators: Definition 2.1 (initial data: connected d-dimensional Riemannian manifold, vacuum constraints, no completeness); Definition 2.2 (extension); Definitions 2.3/2.4 (CGHD); Theorem 2.6 (local existence/uniqueness input, credited to Choquet-Bruhat 1952); Theorem 2.7 (Global uniqueness: common extension containing both GHDs); Theorem 2.8 (MGHD); Lemma 3.1 (isometric-immersion first-jet rigidity, proof read in full); Corollary 3.2; Lemma 3.3; Theorem 3.4 (MCGHD by union); Theorem 3.6 (no corresponding boundary points; proof structure read)
relevance: Vacuum template of the common-extension argument; Lemma 3.1 is field-independent and is reused verbatim in Corollary C's identification layer. Its Theorem 2.7 is replaced, not used, in the coupled corollary.
assumptions: Smooth vacuum Einstein equations; connected initial manifold; time-oriented GHDs.
conclusion: Two vacuum GHDs of the same data admit a common extension (Thm 2.7); an MGHD exists without Zorn's lemma (Thm 2.8).
proof_status: Statements and key lemmas verified verbatim this session; matches the review lane's earlier full-text record (screening-repair-review/sources.jsonl id screening-sbierski-2015-vacuum-common-development). Vacuum only - does not compare matter fields (the review's gate, now closed by scalar-ext-ringstrom-2009-esi-book).
open_questions: Dezornification for coupled systems (see RESULT.md section 6)
limits: ar5iv rendering; published pagination not verified. Vacuum theory only.

title: Wave Equations on Lorentzian Manifolds and Quantization
version: arXiv:0806.1036 (ar5iv rendering of v1), accessed 2026-10-29; review lane record gives PDF pp. 76-87 for the same locators (arXiv:0806.1036v1, 5 June 2008)
locators: Corollary 3.2.4: a smooth solution u of P u = 0 on a globally hyperbolic (M,g) with zero value and zero normal derivative along a smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface S vanishes on M; its use in Theorem 3.2.11's uniqueness step read; foliation input Theorem 1.3.13 referenced by the proof.
relevance: Fixed-background linear uniqueness used to re-derive scalar preservation on any common metric development (RESULT.md section 3.3), and to show the field value is fixed by the data once the metric development is identified.
assumptions: Normally hyperbolic operator P = connection-d'Alembert + B; smooth GH Lorentzian manifold; smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface.
conclusion: Homogeneous uniqueness from zero Cauchy data (arbitrary smooth solution form, not only compactly supported data).
proof_status: Statement and proof opening verified verbatim this session; consistent with the review lane's full-text record (screening-repair-review/sources.jsonl id screening-baer-ginoux-pfaeffle-2008-wave-equations).
limits: Linear theory on a fixed background; no coupled statement.

title: Lorentzian causality theory
version: Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3; springer PDF accessed 2026-10-29
locators: Definition 2.130 (edge of an achronal set, edge(S) subset S); Definition 3.35 (partial Cauchy hypersurface = acausal edgeless, hence closed; Cauchy hypersurface); Theorem 3.45 (for S closed achronal, Int D(S) is globally hyperbolic; attributed by the text to Penrose 1972 Prop. 5.14 and Geroch 1970 Prop. 6; label verified via its invocations in Theorem 3.50 and Section 6 proofs); Theorem 3.50 (closed achronal S: Int D(S) GH; if S is a partial Cauchy hypersurface then D(S) = Int D(S) is open GH with S Cauchy); Remark 3.51 (disk example showing the hypothesis matters); definitions of D^+(S)/D(S) (causal version) and D(S) (timelike version), Section 'Domains of dependence'; Theorem 4.123 (Avez-Seifert) relied on at the review lane's verified locator, not re-read this session.
relevance: Source for the exact domain-of-dependence statement (G) needed on the matched side: openness + global hyperbolicity + Cauchy property of D(K) requires K closed/edgeless (partial Cauchy hypersurface), not merely smooth-spacelike-acausal without intrinsic boundary. This is the gap isolated in RESULT.md section 3.2.
assumptions: Time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime; causal-domain-of-dependence definitions; piecewise C1 curves.
conclusion: as per locators; in particular the closedness hypothesis is operative for the D(K) theorem used by the repaired argument.
proof_status: Definitions and Theorem 3.50 read verbatim; Theorem 3.45's statement verified through its two in-text invocations (its own header did not survive PDF text extraction); proofs of 3.45/3.50 not re-derived. Original sources Penrose 1972 Prop. 5.14 / Geroch 1970 Prop. 6 not independently fetched (gate).
